property_summary: InvMutTest asserts that when addToBalance is called multiple times, the balance after all calls equals the sum of the individual amounts sent, rather than being overwritten by the last call.
After calling addToBalance twice with amounts a1 and a2, the balance of the test contract equals the sum a1 + a2.

After calling addToBalance with amounts a1 and a2, the user balance equals a1 + a2.

After any sequence of addToBalance calls, each user's balance must equal the sum of all msg.value sent by that user; the mutant sets the balance to only the last msg.value, so sending multiple times leaves a balance different from the sum.

After the addToBalance transaction completes, the caller's balance in the reference contract is always at least the Ether sent, but in the mutant it can be lower due to reentrant withdrawal within the same transaction.
After any sequence of calls to addToBalance, the contract's total Ether balance is always at least the sum of all user balances tracked in userBalance.

After a call to addToBalance, the user's balance in the reference contract cannot decrease below its prior value; the mutant allows reentrant withdrawal during addToBalance, leading to a balance decrease.

After a call to addToBalance, the userBalance of the caller plus the contract's Ether balance is invariant; the mutant breaks this by allowing reentrant withdrawal during addToBalance that drains Ether without reducing the caller's stored balance.

For any caller with an initial balance B, after a call to addToBalance with value V, the caller's balance is B+V; the bug breaks this if a reentrant withdrawal is triggered via the same caller's receive function.
getBalance returns the exact ETH sent via addToBalance minus any fully withdrawn balance

After any sequence of calls to addToBalance, the contract never becomes re-entrant—calling withdrawBalance via a re-entrant receive never succeeds in draining more than the caller's own balance; the bug allows a re-entrant call to withdrawBalance while addToBalance is still executing, letting an attacker drain funds twice.

After any external call sequence, the sum of all user balances equals the contract's Ether balance; the bug allows reentrant addToBalance to inflate a user's balance without depositing matching Ether, breaking this invariant.

For every externally triggered execution, the nonReentrant_ guard must prevent re-entrance into addToBalance, ensuring the locked_ flag is set during the guarded call; the bug removes the require check, so no flag is set on entry, and a re-entrant call to addToBalance from withdrawBalance can execute while the flag would have prevented it in the correct contract—causing the contract to break the property that locked_ is never observed false across re-entrant calls.

After any sequence of calls, no user's balance can exceed the total Ether received by the contract; the bug allows reentrant addToBalance during withdrawBalance to increment a user's balance without a corresponding Ether deposit, breaking this invariant.

For any sequence of external calls, the contract's total Ether balance equals the sum of all user balances; the bug allows re-entrant addToBalance to increment a user's balance without a corresponding Ether deposit, breaking this invariant.

After any sequence of external calls through addToBalance and withdrawBalance, a successful addToBalance must still be possible (the nonReentrant modifier must remain usable); the bug locks the contract forever after the first nonReentrant use, making subsequent calls revert.

The total ETH balance of contract C never exceeds the sum of all user balances (recorded in userBalance mapping) because the nonReentrant modifier prevents reentrancy during withdrawals. The buggy mutant removes the lock, allowing reentrant calls to withdrawBalance that drain extra ETH, making the contract balance less than the sum of user balances after withdrawals.

The total ETH balance of C is always at least the sum of its internal userBalance mapping entries. The mutant's missing lock allows a re-entrant attacker to drain more than its recorded balance, making the contract balance lower than the sum of user balances.
